proved_step:
statement: Let ψ:Q→T be an injection, |Q|=m and |T|=N. For any family F of pairs of maps T→T preserving ψ(Q), at most min(|F|,N^(2m)) distinct pairs of induced maps on Q arise.
proof: Each map T→T is determined on ψ(Q) by a restriction with at most N^m possibilities. Thus there are at most N^(2m) pairs of restrictions. Conjugating each restriction by ψ and ψ⁻¹ uniquely determines its induced map on Q. The number of induced pairs is also at most |F|, proving the bound.
gap: This exact multiplicity bound does not show a strict asymptotic improvement for any relevant circuit family.
reopen_if: Specify a circuit family and parameter regime where the restriction bound strictly improves the union count, or give a matching construction.
